items: Seven fertiliser makers agree to pay 50% more for gas, $12.75 per mmBtu and $175 mn upfront, in return for exporting their full output until early January → the state recovers some LNG costs while producers keep selling urea at about $535 a tonne; gas cuts of 20-40% stay.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,200 on Monday but the EGX70 drops 3.76% and the EGX100 2.88% → small caps sell off while Edita (+7.4%) and Telecom Egypt (+5.2%) hold up the blue-chip index.
Edita posts record quarterly revenue of EGP 7.3 bn, up 32.9%, with profit up 41.5% → volume growth and pricing lift the snack maker, and the stock jumps 7.44%.
Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd move three more Gemini services back to the Suez Canal from December → more Asia-Europe traffic adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Egypt raises the private-sector minimum wage 21% to EGP 8,500 a month from 1 January 2027, covering about 26.5 mn workers → higher wages lift consumer spending but raise costs for labour-heavy industries.
TMG Holding's nine-month profit rises 11.9% to EGP 11.72 bn, Fawry's 32% and Edita's 54% → earnings season keeps delivering growth for EGX blue chips.
ONE's container ship crosses the Suez Canal and three more Premier Alliance services are set to follow → the return of Asian carriers adds to canal revenue and dollar inflows.
EGX30 rises 0.31% to 52,187 on Sunday, led by Orascom Construction (+3.4%) and AMOC (+4.8%) → the index is up 24.8% this year, though turnover runs 17% below its 90-day average.

Egypt's final IMF review moves to virtual talks with about $2.3 bn at stake before the programme ends on 15 December → the Cairo mission ended without a staff-level deal; a miss would delay funds and could unsettle the pound.
Telecom Egypt's nine-month profit jumps 43.7% to EGP 24.38 bn and Elsewedy Electric's rises 20.7% to EGP 15.30 bn → two large listed companies report strong growth ahead of Sunday's session.

An ENGIE-led group with Orascom Construction closes $588 mn of debt for a 900 MW wind farm at Ras Shokeir → the project doubles the group's wind capacity in Egypt and gives Orascom a construction contract.
Iran says it targets a US base in Bahrain again as Saudi forces down Houthi drones; Brent ends the week at $96.13 → Gulf attacks keep oil high and Egypt's energy bill under pressure.

Trump says the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and tells Vance to drop the talks, while the blockade stays → the end of diplomacy keeps Gulf energy at risk; oil ends the week at $96.13 and European gas jumps 12%.
European gas surges 12% in a week to €96.18/MWh, and Goldman sees €150 in early 2027 if Gulf LNG stays disrupted → costlier LNG raises Egypt's energy import bill and costs for gas-heavy industry.
Gold has its worst week since March, down 4.7%, and 21K gold in Egypt falls 2.7% to EGP 5,950 a gram → markets see a December Fed hike as certain, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 ends the week at 52,023, up about 1.7% (derived), led by banks → QNB Egypt rises four sessions in a row and Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% on Thursday.

Brent jumps 3.3% to $95.82 on Thursday after Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites and Iran's attack on a US radar in Bahrain → renewed attacks on Gulf energy put oil back near $96, a cost for Egypt's import bill.
Gold falls to a 13-month low and is down 3.5% this week; 21K gold in Egypt drops to about EGP 5,975 a gram → markets fully price a December Fed hike, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 falls 0.91% to 52,023 on Thursday, while Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% → blue chips take profits after a strong week; banks with earnings news still rise.
Suez Canal Bank's nine-month profit rises 12.9% to EGP 5.7 bn as interest income grows about 43% → high rates keep lifting bank income.

stories.h: Misr Life Insurance sets a 15% EGX offering for December
stories.what: Misr Insurance Holding, owned by the Sovereign Fund of Egypt, will sell 750 mn existing shares, or 15% of Misr Life Insurance, through a private placement and a local retail offering, with subscription and trading expected in December. EFG Hermes is sole bookrunner, the remaining 85% faces a lock-up, and the company aims to pay out 70% of FY2026 net income. Its CEO calls it "the first major listing of an ins. company on the EGX."
stories.why: The IMF wants about $1.5 bn from asset sales before the programme ends; Banque du Caire has delivered $658 mn.
stories.aff: The state's privatisation programme, IMF funding and EGX depth.
stories.eg: Meeting the asset-sale target helps unlock the final IMF funds.
stories.egx: Bullish for EFG Holding and market breadth; new supply may weigh on insurers and financials.

stories.h: EGX30 falls 0.99% as small caps slide for a second day
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Arab Finance; EnterpriseAM
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.99% to 51,681.62 on Tuesday, the EGX70 2.42% and the EGX100 2.03%; market cap drops to EGP 4.09 tn on turnover of EGP 9.42 bn. Egyptians net sell EGP 194.6 mn while Arabs and foreigners buy. Palm Hills (-3.46%), Fawry (-2.81%) and Eastern (-2.04%) lead the table's losses. Separately, Qalaa Holdings' Q3 net income rises to EGP 2.7 bn from EGP 81.4 mn on a record EGP 65.9 bn of revenue.
stories.why: Local investors sell; the sources give no single trigger.
stories.aff: Small caps, retail investors and blue chips.
stories.eg: The index is still up 23.6% this year, EnterpriseAM says.
stories.egx: Bearish in the short term for small and mid caps.
stories.names: Palm Hills, Fawry, Eastern (down); EFG Holding (flat).

key.l: Arab Energy Fund's tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive

stories.h: Arab Energy Fund files a $70 mn tender offer for 21.3% of Maridive
stories.what: The Riyadh-based Arab Energy Fund offers $0.70 a share for 100 mn shares of Maridive & Oil Services, a 44% premium to the six-month average before July's announcement but about 1% above Monday's close. The FRA is reviewing the offer. Maridive's first-half net income rises to $48.61 mn from $10.89 mn.
stories.why: The fund first flagged its interest in July, and Maridive's first-half profit more than quadrupled.
stories.aff: Maridive's shareholders and EGX energy-services valuations.
stories.eg: Gulf capital keeps flowing into EGX-listed companies.
stories.egx: Bullish for Maridive; little upside left at the current price.

stories.h: Gold drops below $3,800 as Fed officials signal more hikes
stories.what: Spot gold falls 1.5% to $3,790.18 on Wednesday as St. Louis Fed President Musalem says several more hikes may be needed and New York Fed President Williams says there is more work to do. Markets price quarter-point hikes in December and January. Gold has lost more than a quarter of its value since the war began in February. In Egypt, Banky puts 21K gold at EGP 5,900 a gram.
stories.why: War-driven energy costs keep inflation high, so central banks tighten and real yields rise.
stories.aff: Local gold prices, the dollar and emerging-market carry.
stories.eg: Cheaper gold for Egyptian savers; a firmer dollar is a risk for the pound.

stories.h: Oil slips as US crude stocks build despite Gulf attacks
stories.what: Brent falls 61 cents to $92.53 and WTI $1.24 to $84.77 on Wednesday morning after API data show US crude stocks up 5.28 mn barrels. US-Iran strikes, Iranian attacks in Bahrain and Houthi drone strikes on Saudi pumping stations limit the fall. Vanda Insights' Vandana Hari cites "a chorus of analysts forecasting a sizeable market surplus."
stories.why: Surplus forecasts outweigh supply risks in the Gulf.
stories.aff: Egypt's fuel import bill and the pound.
stories.eg: Brent near $92 eases Egypt's energy costs.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for importers and energy users.

stories.h: Board of Peace warns the Gaza ceasefire could collapse
stories.what: The US-backed Board of Peace tells the UN Security Council the Israel-Hamas truce may collapse without steps to carry out the 2025 deal. It says Israel blocks the interim civil administration for Gaza, and supply restrictions and funding gaps hurt winter preparations. "A ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely," the board says.
stories.why: Both sides fall short of their ceasefire commitments, the board says.
stories.aff: Regional stability on Egypt's border and reconstruction plans.
stories.eg: A collapse would raise security risks on Egypt's border and delay reconstruction work.
stories.egx: Neutral; a renewed war would weigh on tourism sentiment.
